notes.body:
Tirzepatide body model
Physiological based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model of tirzepatide in Human.
Tirzepatide is given subcutaneously: the dose enters a depot, from which the fraction Fsc_tir (the absolute bioavailability, 80 %) is absorbed into the venous plasma and the rest is degraded at the injection site to the metabolites. Tirzepatide is bound to albumin (99 %) and distributes with it into the interstitial space of the tissues (ftissue_tir, Kp_tir). It is eliminated by proteolytic cleavage of the peptide backbone and beta-oxidation of the C20 fatty diacid (TIR2TM), which scales with the body weight; tirzepatide itself is not excreted. The metabolites are excreted in the urine with a clearance relative to the glomerular filtration rate (kidney submodel) and in the bile (liver submodel), from where they reach the feces through an intestinal transit chain (intestine submodel).
The metabolites are one species counted in tirzepatide equivalents (the molecular weight of tirzepatide), which is what the measurements of the radiolabel are (ng-eq/ml, % of the dose). They keep the C20 fatty diacid and distribute into a slow tissue pool (ftissue_tm, Kp_tm), from which they return to the plasma and are excreted over weeks: tirzepatide is about 80 % of the radioactivity in plasma, while the excretion of the radiolabel lags behind the cleavage (Martin2024).
The content of this model has been carefully created in a manual research effort.

The absolute bioavailability of a subcutaneous dose of tirzepatide, 80 % (label, EMA assessment report). The rest of the depot is degraded at the injection site to the metabolites, which are excreted (Martin2024: 99 % of the radiolabel recovered).

parameter.name: clearance of the cleavage of tirzepatide

body.p: The clearance at the reference body weight BW_ref, it scales with the body weight as the volumes do, so that the half-life does not depend on the body weight (about 5 days in lean and obese subjects). The cleavage takes place in the plasma and the tissues; with an exchange much faster than the elimination its location does not change the timecourses, it is lumped in the venous plasma.
The value of TIR2TM_k is the result of the fit PK_20261019_095941__4f772, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

body.p: Renal function relative to the healthy glomerular filtration rate GFR_base, which is 101 ml/min at 75 kg; a measured creatinine clearance or eGFR of X ml/min is the renal function X/101.

parameter.name: renal clearance of the tirzepatide metabolites relative to the GFR

body.p: The renal clearance of the metabolites of tirzepatide is TMEX_f times the GFR. The metabolites carry the C20 fatty diacid and the linker of tirzepatide and are largely bound to albumin, so that their clearance is a small fraction of the GFR. Tirzepatide itself is not excreted in the urine (Martin2024: no intact tirzepatide in urine or feces).
The value of KI__TMEX_f is the result of the fit PK_20261019_095941__4f772, its uncertainty is the profile likelihood of the fit.

parameter.name: rate of the biliary excretion of the tirzepatide metabolites

body.p: The biliary clearance of the metabolites is TMBEX_k times the volume of the liver.

parameter.name: rate of the intestinal transit of the tirzepatide metabolites

body.p: The rate per step of the transit chain from the intestinal lumen into the feces; the mean transit time is (1 + n_chain)/TMEXC_k = 50 hr, the whole gut transit time of about 2 days. Not fitted: the cumulative recovery in the feces (Martin2024) does not identify it (profile likelihood flat over a mean transit of 12 hr to 5 days).
